key_insight: RayPE replaces purely 2D/temporal token positions with ray-space geometry, so video models can reason about the 3D structure implied by camera rays. Its core idea is that the relationship between two rays can be encoded with a bilinear Plücker reciprocal product, closely matching how attention already computes pairwise interactions.
problem_solved: Standard video diffusion transformers use RoPE over the (u, v, t) sampling grid, which describes where pixels come from but not how they relate in 3D space. This makes it harder for the model to capture viewpoint-consistent geometry and scene structure across frames.
method: Extend positional encoding from image-plane/time coordinates to ray-space representations derived from camera rays.
Use the Plücker reciprocal product to encode geometric relations between rays in a bilinear form aligned with Transformer attention.
Inject the ray-space encoding into video diffusion transformers to improve 3D-aware generation.
impact: For practitioners, RayPE offers a geometry-aware way to improve video generation without changing the core Transformer paradigm. It is especially useful for view-consistent, scene-aware, and 3D-correct video synthesis tasks.

paper_title: RayPE: Ray-Space Positional Encoding for 3D-Aware Video Generation
paper_authors: Minghao Yin, Jiahao Lu, Wenbo Hu, Wang Zhao, Shan Ying
